title: Object Relations Theory
originAuthor: Donald Winnicott, Melanie Klein, Ronald Fairbairn
summary: The self develops through early relational experience. When caregiving is 'good enough,' the True Self emerges; when it fails, a False Self forms as protective adaptation. Internal representations of relationships (objects) shape all later relating.

content.title: Core Concept
content.content: Object Relations Theory proposes that the self is formed through early relationships with caregivers ('objects'). Winnicott distinguished between the True Self — spontaneous, authentic, alive — and the False Self — compliant, adaptive, protective. The False Self develops when caregiving fails to meet the infant's spontaneous gestures with adequate response. It is not pathology but survival: the child builds what works to maintain connection.

content.title: How TEG-Blue Integrates This
content.content: TEG-Blue translates Winnicott into nervous system terms. The baseline emotional-somatic configuration is present at birth — innate rhythms, sensitivities, and awareness capacities in proto-form. The adaptive identity is the cognitive-behavioural structure built when authentic expression was not safe. Framework 2 maps this formation process: how unpredictable, incongruent, or invalidating environments shape identity as protection rather than expression.
